name: Myriad Landscape
oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {C}.
{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this land: Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
blocked_sentences: {2}, {T}, Sacrifice this land: Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

needs.what: a way for a multi-card `search_library` to constrain the picked cards against *each other* -- e.g. a `share_subtype: true` (or `share: "subtypes"`) key on the search spec that, once the first card is chosen, restricts the remaining choices to cards sharing a subtype with it, so "up to two basic land cards that share a land type" fetches Forest+Forest or Island+Island but never Forest+Swamp
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Every selector clause is evaluated per candidate in isolation (`_matches_in_zone` runs the selector against one oid at a time), so `types`/`supertypes`/`subtypes` can only say "each card is a basic land", not "the two cards match one another". The nearest clause, `shares_a_type_with`, compares a candidate against an object already in `ctx.bindings` by name -- but nothing binds a card the same search is in the middle of choosing, and `search_library` has no bind/output key at all. Splitting it into two searches is a different card: it shuffles twice, is two separate search events, and each search carries its own independent "up to" count, so the second pick would still be unconstrained. `subtypes: ["Forest"]` and friends would hardcode one land type, which the printed card leaves to the player.
